document.about: Western Digital WD Gold data sheet (4 pages). Its body text footnotes capacities and workloads with a note number raised right after the quantity.

notes: 2026-11-23 (#79): a raised number after a quantity stayed in it, so 26TB with note 1 read 26TB1. After a quantity it is a note, unless it squares or cubes a unit of length.
2026-11-24 (#100): each page's first capacity in its spec table, `26TB`, `16TB`, `8TB`, was taken for its folio. The sheet prints no page numbers.

2026-11-24 (#147): the spec table's `Power Management` band stands directly over its `Average power requirements (W)` band, and each data row took only the nearest band as its `doc:sectionLabel`, so `Power Management` was on no cell. A row carries the bands set directly over each other, joined from the top down.

checks.issue: Note 1 was read into the capacity: up to 26TB1. (#322: a note's number is now written raised, `up to 26TB¹`.)
As above, for note 2 on the workload: 550TB2 per year. (#322: a note's number is now written raised, `550TB² per year`.)
A drive capacity was the page's folio.
The power rows' cells carried only `Average power requirements (W)`; `Power Management` reached no cell.
